Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Kurt Seifried
Message:
feat: drive labels — what a document is classified as, read-only by construction (#263)

* feat: drive labels - what a document is classified as, read-only by construction

Ships list_labels, the last security-adjacent item on the 1.0.0 inventory. 39
tools, up from 38.

ADDS AN OAUTH SCOPE: drive.labels.readonly. Existing tokens do not carry it and
the existing re-consent detection will prompt for a fresh sign-in. It also needs
drivelabels.googleapis.com enabled in the Cloud project, because a granted scope
is not API enablement - the trap already recorded for Docs/Sheets/Slides.

It takes two APIs, and that is the difficulty. Drive v3's files.listLabels says
WHICH labels are on a file but not what they are called: the Label it returns is
{id, revisionId, fields}, no title, and selection values are opaque choice ids
too. Only the separate Drive Labels API turns bXlsYWJlbA into "Confidential". So
doc.labels is a join - one list call, then one definition per applied label, which
for a real document is one or two calls.

Read-only BY CONSTRUCTION, not by configuration: this library never requests the
drive.labels write scope, so there is no capability to enable and no configuration
in which a model can change a classification. Labels are what DLP and retention
key on, so setting one is not an edit to a document, it is a claim about how the
organisation must treat it - and unlike a bad edit, nobody sees a diff.

Names can be unavailable, and that must never look like "unlabelled". The API may
be off, or the token may predate the scope. In both cases the ids are still TRUE,
so failing would discard real information and returning nothing would report a
classified document as unclassified - the error somebody acts on. Labels come back
with name=None and an unresolved_reason naming which cause and its fix; the two
are told apart because an operator who reads "enable the API" when the problem is
a stale token will enable it and still see no names.

And an id is never presented as a name. The first draft got this wrong for
selection values - with no definition they fell through to str(v) and returned the
bare choice id, exactly the failure the module was written to prevent. A test
caught it before it shipped.

tests/test_auth.py loses its "the read-write set contains no .readonly scope"
assertion. That rule was a proxy for "a posture must not silently ask for less
than it claims"; labels break the proxy without breaking the rule, so the
assertion is now specific: exactly one read-only scope, and it is that one.

Verified by falsification: dropping unresolvable labels fails 8 tests,
maxResults->pageSize fails 1 (Google IGNORES the wrong name, so a heavily-labelled
file would silently truncate), LABEL_VIEW_FULL->BASIC fails 1.

Suite 1500 passed, 12 skipped; coverage 88.98% and 100% on the new module; ruff
and mypy clean.

* docs: record 0.33.0 as published

The release checker caught it: v0.33.0 was tagged, uploaded and verified on PyPI,
and its changelog heading still said "not released". Both halves of the check
fired - a tag should mean released, and a version people can install should say
so in the changelog.

The heading loses "not released" and 0.33.0 joins the On PyPI line. The habit is
mark-pending, publish, then flip; the flip is the step that gets skipped, which is
exactly why the check exists.
